text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam received the General Secretary of France's Foreign Ministry, Bertrand Dufourcq in Hanoi on Monday. Dufourcq said France would continue to support Vietnam's reform process.

-- An International Monetary Fund (IMF) team held preliminary discussion on Vietnam's economic programme for the remaining $180 million of a three-year enhanced structural adjustment facility (ESAF) to be released.

-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment has officially suggested that the government invest in two large television projects worth $240 million between now and 2005. Under the plans, a $197.5 million television centre and antenna tower would be built in Hanoi. - - - -

-- A Canadian Vietnamese was sentenced to death and her Vietnamese mother was sentenced to life in prison on Monday for trafficking heroin. They have 15 days to appeal agaisnt the ruling. Alternatively, they may send a letter to President Le Duc Anh within 7 days requesting clemency.
-- Central Vietnam's Ham Rong bridge, an important target of American bombing during the war which ended in 1975, will be rebuilt in the second half of 1997 with funds from the OECF.
